title: RovingFocusGroup
summary: Moving focus inside a toolbar, a set of options or a grid with a hardware keyboard is done by the Compose focus system. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Nothing is needed for standard controls: Tab moves between focusable elements and the arrow keys move focus in their direction. Wrap a set of controls in focusGroup() so Tab treats it as one stop in the traversal order, add focusRestorer() so focus returns to the last focused item, and use a FocusRequester to move focus in code.
whenNotToUse: Do not make every item of a long list or grid focusable by hand; lazy lists and grids take part in focus search themselves. Do not intercept the arrow keys unless the group has a custom order the layout does not express.

states.name: focused item
states.description: The focused control draws its own focus indication (Monarch controls draw the focus ring).

appearance: No appearance of its own: focus is drawn by each control, and Monarch controls draw the focus ring in the focus-ring color of the theme.
platformNotes: The web needs RovingFocusGroup because a browser puts every control in the Tab order and gives the arrow keys no meaning; it keeps one tabindex=0 item and moves it with the arrows, Home and End. On Android with a hardware keyboard, Compose moves focus with the arrow keys by two-dimensional search, and focusGroup() makes a set of controls one stop for Tab. focusRestorer() returns to the last focused item, which is what the roving tabindex achieves. The web's loop and Home/End have no built-in equivalent; add onPreviewKeyEvent on the group if a toolbar needs them. Only matters with a hardware keyboard or a D-pad. iOS uses its focus engine in the same way.
accessibility: System behavior: Tab and Shift+Tab move between focus groups and focusable elements in layout order; the arrow keys move focus to the nearest element in their direction.
TalkBack does not use keyboard focus: it moves through elements by swiping, so focus groups change nothing for it.
With focusRestorer, Tab back into the group focuses the item that was focused last.
edgeCases: focusRestorer needs the items to have stable identity; in a lazy list give each item a key.
requestFocus() throws when the FocusRequester is not attached to a composed element; call it from an event or after composition.

examples.title: Toolbar
examples.template:
Row(
    modifier = Modifier
        .focusRestorer()
        .focusGroup()
        .semantics { contentDescription = {{label}} },
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space1),
) {
    MonarchButton(text = {{buttons.0.label}}, onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm)
    MonarchButton(text = {{buttons.1.label}}, onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm)
    MonarchButton(
        text = {{buttons.2.label}},
        onClick = {},
        variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost,
        size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
        enabled = !{{buttons.2.disabled}},
    )
    MonarchButton(text = {{buttons.3.label}}, onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm)
}
examples.code:
Row(
    modifier = Modifier
        .focusRestorer()
        .focusGroup()
        .semantics { contentDescription = "Text formatting" },
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space1),
) {
    MonarchButton(text = "Bold", onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm)
    MonarchButton(text = "Italic", onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm)
    MonarchButton(
        text = "Strikethrough",
        onClick = {},
        variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost,
        size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm,
        enabled = !true,
    )
    MonarchButton(text = "Link", onClick = {}, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Ghost, size = MonarchButtonSize.Sm)
}
